cards.name: Paste without Formatting
cards.summary: Pastes clipboard text into the type layer being edited without the source's font, size, colour or styling, so it takes on the style at the insertion point. Disabled in every scratch state the harvest tried, including one with a text layer active but not in edit mode; none of those states entered text editing or put text on the clipboard, so it most likely needs both (inferred, not tested).
use_for: pasting copy from a Word doc or web page into a poster headline without dragging in its font
dropping client-supplied text into a styled social-card template and keeping the template's type style
refreshing body text in a menu or flyer layout without restyling each paste
avoid: pasting images or layers: use Edit > Paste, or Edit > Paste Special > Paste in Place
scripted text replacement: set the type layer's textItem.contents instead (unverified: expected to keep the layer's existing type style)
cards.script_api: None found by the harvest (no menuItemType or event matches). Same job from a script (unverified): app.activeDocument.activeLayer.textItem.contents = "..." on a LayerKind.TEXT layer keeps that layer's existing style.

review.changes: summary: the enabling condition (type edit mode + text on the clipboard) is now marked as inferred: the harvest fixtures never entered text editing or copied text; confidence high -> medium for that reason; avoid: Paste in Place is Edit > Paste Special > Paste in Place; textItem.contents style claim marked unverified

cards.name: Perspective Warp
cards.summary: Interactive perspective editing for one layer: in Layout mode you draw planes (quads) over the image and align their edges to its architecture, then in Warp mode you drag the corner pins to change the viewing angle while lines stay straight. Needs an open document with a single layer active (disabled for groups and multiple layers), the graphics processor enabled, and a person to draw the planes.
cards.how: Layout: drag to draw a plane and snap its edges to the building or box sides; draw a second plane against the first to join them along an edge. Warp: drag pins, Shift-click an edge to straighten it, or use the automatic straighten / level buttons on the options bar; press Enter or the check mark to commit.
use_for: fixing the camera angle of a building photo for a property flyer
matching a product shot's perspective to a background plate before compositing
flattening a sign or packaging face so a new label can be placed on it
avoid: a single flat face such as a screen or poster mock-up: Edit > Transform > Perspective or Distort is quicker
lens barrel or keystone correction from camera metadata: use Filter > Lens Correction or Camera Raw Geometry
unattended pipelines: the command waits for planes drawn by hand
cards.script_api: runMenuItem(stringIDToTypeID('perspectiveWarpTransform')) (terminology menuItemType label match, not run): it would enter the interactive Layout mode and wait for a person. Do not call executeAction('perspectiveWarpTransform') with an empty descriptor: the same call for Puppet Warp (rigidTransform) left Photoshop in its interactive mode and hung the script bridge. Unattended (unverified): replay a ScriptListener-recorded perspectiveWarpTransform descriptor (Photoshop's terminology lists the event's keys: mode, referenceRect, vertices, warpedVertices, quads, constrainedSides) with DialogModes.NO, behind a timeout.

review.changes: equivalents: removed AI Free Distort and CDR Add Perspective: those are the counterparts of Edit > Transform > Distort / Perspective (their own cards say so, and this card's avoid line sends single-face jobs there); neither app has a multi-plane perspective warp; how: dropped the invented options-bar button names; script_api: added the empty-descriptor hang warning (sibling rigidTransform hung) and the event's terminology keys for the unattended route

Enabled with no document open.
cards.how: The choices that matter most: File Handling (JPEG / HEIC / TIFF: automatically open all supported, open with settings, or disable), where image settings are saved (sidecar .xmp files keep edits with the raw file), Raw Defaults (Adobe Default, Camera Settings or a preset) and the graphics processor setting.
use_for: stopping JPEGs from opening in Camera Raw when a batch of product shots should go straight into Photoshop
making every raw file open with the studio's base preset for consistent catalogue colour
keeping edits in sidecar XMP files so a photographer's adjustments travel with the raw files
avoid: editing one photo's look: open it in Filter > Camera Raw Filter or the Camera Raw dialog
Photoshop's own file and save options: use Edit > Preferences > File Handling

cards.name: Puppet Warp
cards.summary: Interactive pin-based bending of one layer: Photoshop lays a triangle mesh over the layer's content, you click to add pins and drag them to bend limbs, tails, text or objects while pinned areas stay put. On a Smart Object it is applied as an editable Smart Filter. Needs an open document with a single layer active (disabled for groups and multiple layers) and a person to place and drag the pins.
cards.how: Options bar: Mode (Rigid, Normal, Distort), Density (Fewer Points, Normal, More Points), Expansion (how far the mesh extends past the edge), Show Mesh, Pin Depth (which part overlaps), Rotate (Auto or Fixed; Alt-drag near a pin to rotate around it). Press Enter to commit.
use_for: bending a cut-out arm, scarf or tail into a new pose for a composite
curving a cut-out product or ribbon to follow a layout path on a poster
small posture fixes on a model cut-out without redrawing
avoid: unattended scripts: the harvest's empty-descriptor call hung Photoshop in this mode and needed a force-restart
even, overall shape changes: use Edit > Transform > Warp, or Filter > Liquify for face and body shaping
